pilot_metadata.purpose: Test whether the Decision Work Brief shape names a concrete action consequence in a different decision type without hiding source thinness.

selected_case.selection_reason: Preferred PR119 case was available as a completed run and differs from the first founder/cofounder governance case; this one is a go-to-market, enterprise-launch, and runway decision.

input_scope.semantic_support_policy: Codex-assisted interpretation used the PR115 metadata-only packet for source availability and custody, plus local metadata-only Decision Trail and Decision Work Receipt summaries. Private source text was not copied into this artifact.
input_scope.pilot_size_reason: Exactly one additional completed run; PR119 is a second tiny case, not a batch.

human_followup_questions: Did the 900-person prospect actually offer payment, procurement clarity, and tolerance for the team's support and audit-log constraints?
Would keeping the enterprise beta private weaken fundraising or recruiting more than the safe structured artifacts can show?
Which buyer would accept the written pilot shape without forcing mature-vendor promises the company cannot yet keep?
second_case_brief.action_consequence_read: Provisional read: the team would stop treating the 900-person logo or public launch as the default path, give both prospects the same paid and scoped private-pilot offer, and award priority to the buyer whose behavior creates usable cash or proof within explicit stop rules.
second_case_brief.missingness_or_uncertainty_read: The checked-in-safe packet does not include raw conversation, raw revised answer, raw memo, provider text, or private ledgers, so starting-direction overlap, buyer reality, board pressure, and lost-value severity remain uncertain.
second_case_brief.lost_value_or_possible_noise_note: The brief may overcorrect against public optics: a public page could matter for fundraising or recruiting if it answers a concrete investor or talent question that the safe artifacts cannot evaluate.

notes: Codex-assisted provisional second tiny case draft for PR119.
Checked-in safe summary only; no generator, runtime integration, human validation, product proof, or model-call code exists in this PR.

value.decision_story_read: The decision appears to be whether to launch a public enterprise beta next month to secure enterprise prospects and extend runway, or instead pursue a restricted private enterprise pilot program.
value.why_medium_uncertainty: The decision question is structured, but the checked-in-safe artifact omits raw conversation and private interpretation surfaces.

decision.empty_meaning: If this section is empty, the pilot has not identified the decision being drafted.

value.candidate_starting_direction: The likely starting direction already leaned away from a public launch and toward a private enterprise proof program, with the 900-person prospect prioritized if it accepted strict gates.
value.why_high_uncertainty: The raw baseline and revised answer are not included, so the amount of actual change versus sharpening remains uncertain.

starting_direction.empty_meaning: If this section is empty, the packet did not support a safe read of the starting direction.

value.pressure_read: Lolla appears to have pressed on whether enterprise-logo size, public-launch optics, and generic readiness gates were being treated as evidence before buyer behavior, audit-log limits, support load, and stop rules were specified.
pressed_dimensions: whether the 900-person prospect deserved priority by default
whether public launch answered a concrete investor or recruiting question
whether gates had owners, thresholds, and stop actions
whether brittle audit logs, support load, churn, and seven-month runway should constrain the launch shape

what_lolla_pressed_on.empty_meaning: If this section is empty, the pilot has not identified what Lolla pressured.

value.change_read: The plan changed from favoring the larger logo under strict gates toward making both prospects compete for priority through the same paid, scoped, private pilot shape.
specific_changes: The 900-person company no longer gets the first slot by default.
Both prospects receive the same written pilot shape: paid commitment, one workflow, no public launch, capped support, explicit audit-log boundaries, conversion trigger, and reference terms.
Priority is based on payment, procurement clarity, tolerance for scope, and usefulness as proof.
The public-launch thesis must name the investor or recruiting outcome it actually changes.
Readiness gates become tripwires with owner, threshold, and stop action.

what_changed.empty_meaning: If this section is empty, the pilot has not identified a source-backed change.

value.action_consequence: Before the exec meeting or buyer call, the team would write the same private-pilot offer for both prospects, define stop rules for reliability, audit exports, support load, commercial commitment, and customer response times, and choose the buyer whose behavior creates usable proof.
candidate_next_actions: Do not award priority to the 900-person prospect just because of logo size.
Ask the board observer, investor, and head of sales what concrete outcome a public page changes.
Convert likely failure modes into contract clauses, support caps, and launch limits before the buyer call.
Keep public launch as a later marketing experiment only if private proof and named external outcomes exist.

what_this_means_for_action.empty_meaning: If this section is empty, the pilot has not translated the decision story into action consequence.

missingness_and_uncertainty: The raw conversation, revised answer, memo, live transcript, provider text, and private ledgers are absent from the checked-in artifact.
The safe report marks useful versus noisy friction, lost value, stakeholders, values, and assistant influence as requiring interpretation or not supplied.
The real commercial seriousness of each prospect is not verified here.
The public launch may have fundraising or recruiting value that is not visible from checked-in-safe artifacts.
value.possible_overcorrection_or_noise: The brief may overcorrect away from public optics if a public enterprise page would answer a specific investor or talent question. It could also overcorrect toward the smaller prospect if the larger buyer would accept the company's constraints and create stronger proof.

what_still_might_be_wrong.empty_meaning: If this section is empty, missingness has not been made explicit.

not_proven: The draft does not prove whether the beta should launch.
The draft does not prove the private pilot path is better advice.
The draft does not measure answer quality.
The draft does not authorize agent action.
The draft is not human validated.
Two clean cases do not create general product evidence.

what_was_not_proven.empty_meaning: If this section is empty, the brief is missing required non-claims.

value.receipt_story: The backing layer is the locally generated PR115 metadata-only packet plus local metadata-only Decision Work Receipt and Decision Trail reports. These were used as source/custody context and were not checked in.
available_evidence: Decision Trail decision question, constraints, audit pressure, and structural delta fields
Decision Work Receipt missingness and custody metadata

evidence_receipt.empty_meaning: If this section is empty, readers cannot tell where the supporting receipt and evidence live.

non_claims.empty_meaning: A missing non-claim means the brief is incomplete and may overstate what the audit can support.

did_both_cases_produce_concrete_action_c.detail: The first case named moving authority first and narrowing the transition role; the second names equal paid/scoped private-pilot offers, buyer-behavior priority, and tripwire gates before public launch.

did_both_cases_preserve_uncertainty_and_.detail: Both briefs keep raw/private artifacts out of checked-in outputs and explicitly mark starting direction, lost value, and source-boundary uncertainty.

did_second_case_test_different_decision_.detail: The first case is founder/cofounder operating authority; the second is enterprise go-to-market launch, runway, buyer selection, and product-readiness gating.

did_shape_work_outside_founder_governanc.detail: The brief still names decision, pressure, change, action consequence, remaining uncertainty, non-claims, and evidence refs in a different decision type.

did_renderer_make_second_case_feel_too_c.detail: The Markdown remains orderly and readable, so the high-uncertainty sections and non-claims must stay visible.

schema_or_renderer_gap.detail: The renderer preserves field-key labels and source refs faithfully, which is good for custody but still a little internal for eventual customer-facing prose.

is_one_more_diversity_case_needed_before.detail: A small pattern review over these two different decision types is now more useful than adding a third case immediately; the review can decide whether a third case, renderer patch, or human review comes next.

aggregate_observations.strongest_useful_signal: The Decision Work Brief shape again names a concrete action consequence: do not default to the larger logo or public launch; make both prospects accept the same private paid pilot shape and choose based on evidence-producing buyer behavior.
aggregate_observations.strongest_missingness_thinness_risk: The checked-in-safe artifact cannot verify buyer seriousness, board/investor pressure, true launch-risk tolerance, or whether the starting answer already contained most of the revised action sequence.
aggregate_observations.strongest_overclaim_risk: Two clean rendered briefs can start to look like product evidence even though both are Codex-assisted, non-human-validated, and source-limited.
aggregate_observations.brief_shape_read: The shape worked better than a receipt inventory on a second decision type because it preserved both action consequence and uncertainty.
aggregate_observations.renderer_read: The renderer is adequate for internal review, but field keys and source refs still make it feel like a conservative product-shape artifact rather than polished customer copy.

decision_gate.rationale: Two different decision types produced concrete action-consequence reads while preserving uncertainty and non-claims. The next step should compare the two-case pattern before adding more cases or patching the renderer.

blocked_outcomes.reason: Not an allowed PR119 outcome and not justified from two Codex-assisted checked-in-safe cases.
Human review remains necessary eventually, but the two-case pattern can be reviewed first without broadening.
